name: Analytics & Data Dashboard

designIntent.primaryGoal: Help users detect meaningful change and act on reliable information.
designIntent.visualThesis: Data is the primary content; decoration must not compete with it.

visualDirection.density: medium-to-high, controlled by task and user expertise
visualDirection.surfaces: charts and tables share clear alignment; panels only when they define a meaningful group
visualDirection.colorIntent: color encodes series/status consistently; include redundant labels and patterns where needed
visualDirection.typography: tabular numerals, readable axis labels, explicit units and scales
visualDirection.motion: animate only meaningful data changes and preserve access to static values

layout.pattern: filter/period controls + KPI context + primary visualization + supporting table
layout.spacing: compact, grid-aligned and consistent between chart and table
layout.responsive: provide alternative table or summary when charts cannot fit

accessibility.keyboard: filters, data tables and chart summaries must be reachable
accessibility.reducedMotion: provide stable values and avoid motion-only data comparisons

notes: Do not fabricate data. Clearly distinguish zero, missing, stale and unavailable values.

aiGuidance.primaryFlow: Ask a question → choose scope and time range → detect change → inspect contributing records → decide or export.
prioritize: Time range, filters, units, source and data freshness
A table or record-level explanation behind summary metrics
confirmOrMarkUnknown: Metric definitions, aggregation, timezone and refresh frequency
Whether values are measured, estimated, sampled or synthetic
avoidByDefault: KPI tiles without a decision or comparison
Invented values, units, benchmarks or trend narratives
acceptanceChecks: Charts have a question, units, labelled axes and clear range
Zero, missing, stale and unavailable values are distinct
A table or accessible summary exposes underlying data

compositionEscapes.when: The main job is finding exceptions, unexpected change or operational risk.
compositionEscapes.composition: Start with an exception queue or annotated time series, then show contributing dimensions, baseline and source records for the selected anomaly.
contentRequirements: Baseline, time window and comparison scope

compositionEscapes.when: The user needs to understand one important business or product question over time.
compositionEscapes.composition: Build around one primary metric, its time range and a relevant comparison; place annotations beside the evidence they explain.
contentRequirements: Time period, comparison method and source

compositionEscapes.when: Users work with large datasets, exact values, filtering or record-level follow-up.
compositionEscapes.composition: Use a searchable, sortable table as the main canvas; retain a compact summary only for scope, totals or selected-row context.
contentRequirements: Stable row identity and column definitions
